newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks begin last colonial trade day with gains.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks begin last colonial trade day with gains.

text.p: The last day of trading under colonial rule got off to a strong start in Hong Kong on Friday as investors attempted to give Britain a warm send off.
The blue chip Hang Seng Index jumped 147.52 points, or 0.98 percent, to an early high of 15,275.54 before later paring its gains to trade up 6.64 points at 15,134.66 at late-morning.
Red chips were the favourites as investors looked forward to a new era under China. The China-Affiliated Corporations index surged 86.25 points, or 2.66 percent, to 3,330.94.
"Sentiment is strong and people are aggressively participating in the market ahead of the handover," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"The market focus is on red chips and selectively on blue chips," he said.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of British colonial rule.
To celebrate the historic handover, the stock market will be closed from Monday to Wednesday.
Analysts said some investors were reluctant to keep their positions open until Thursday with the U.S. Federal Reserve set to meet on Tuesday and Wednesday to deliberate interest rates.
With Hong Kong's post-handover government set to announce its policy on housing next week, investors were also cautious on property stocks, they said.
"We are getting closer to the housing policy statement and it's the uncertainty factor that people don't like," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
"We expected a handover rally and we are seeing it in the red chips," he added. "People are focused on red chips today."
The last initial public offering under colonial rule got off to a poor start on Friday, suffering from an oversupply of new issues of late.
Jiangsu Expressway Co Ltd shares opened at HK$2.80, compared with an issue price of HK$3.11, then fell to HK$2.60.
The Hong Kong public offering was only 2.5 times subscribed and the international portion was 12 times subscribed.
Overall market turnover was a robust HK$7.29 billion after the first hour of trade.
